subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When the flux linkage through a coil is at its maximum value, the induced EMF is:
questions.explain: EMF depends on the rate of change of flux linkage; at maximum flux linkage the rate of change is momentarily zero, so the EMF is zero.

questions.q: A transformer's iron core is laminated (made of thin insulated sheets) primarily to:
options: reduce energy losses due to eddy currents
questions.explain: Laminating the core breaks up the paths for eddy currents, reducing the energy they would otherwise dissipate as heat.

questions.q: Lenz's law states that the direction of an induced current is always such that it:
options: opposes the change in flux that produced it
enhances the change in flux that produced it
is independent of the flux change
questions.explain: The induced current opposes the change causing it, which is why Faraday's law carries a minus sign.

questions.q: For a charged particle of mass m and charge q moving at speed v perpendicular to field B, the radius of its circular path is:
questions.explain: Setting Bqv = mv²/r gives r = mv/(Bq).

questions.q: For an ideal transformer, the turns-ratio equation is:
questions.explain: For an ideal transformer V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p.

questions.q: An ideal transformer has 100 turns on the primary and 500 turns on the secondary. If the primary voltage is 12 V, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explain: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p, so V_s = 12 × 500/100 = 60 V (a step-up transformer).

questions.q: An electron (charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) moves at 2.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a 0.50 T field. The magnetic force on it is:
The force on a charge q moving with velocity v at right angles to a field B is given by:
questions.explain: The magnetic force on a moving charge is F = Bqv when v is perpendicular to B.

questions.q: UK mains supply has an rms voltage of about 230 V. Its approximate peak voltage is:
A charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field follows a circular path. The magnetic force does no work on it because:
options: the force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so the speed is unchanged
questions.explain: Since F = Bqv acts perpendicular to v, it changes direction but not speed, so it does no work and the kinetic energy stays constant.

questions.q: The EMF output of an AC generator with a coil rotating at constant speed is:
questions.explain: Uniform rotation produces a sinusoidally varying flux linkage, giving a sinusoidal alternating EMF.

questions.q: A current-carrying conductor experiences zero force in a magnetic field when:
options: it is parallel to the field
the current is at 45° to the field
it is perpendicular to the field
questions.explain: F = BIL sinθ is zero when the conductor (current) is parallel to the field (θ = 0).

questions.q: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced EMF is proportional to the:
options: rate of change of flux linkage
questions.explain: The magnitude of the induced EMF equals the rate of change of flux linkage, ε = −d(NΦ)/dt.

questions.q: The National Grid transmits power at very high voltage mainly to:
options: reduce the current for a given power, lowering I²R heating losses in the cables
increase the resistance of the cables
increase the current and so the power delivered
questions.explain: For a given power, higher voltage means lower current, and since power loss in cables is I²R, lower current greatly reduces resistive heating losses.

questions.q: A magnet is dropped north-pole-down through a vertical coil. As it approaches, the induced current in the coil makes the top of the coil a:
options: north pole, to repel the magnet
south pole, to attract the magnet
south pole, to repel the magnet
north pole, to attract the magnet
questions.explain: By Lenz's law the coil opposes the approaching north pole by presenting a north pole to repel it.

questions.q: For a sinusoidal AC supply, the rms voltage relates to the peak voltage by:
questions.explain: For a sinusoidal waveform, V_rms = V_peak/√2.

questions.q: Magnetic flux Φ through a flat coil of area A in a uniform field B (normal to the coil) is given by:
questions.explain: For a field perpendicular to the area, the flux is Φ = BA.

questions.q: The rms value of an alternating current is significant because it gives:
options: the average value over a half cycle
the equivalent steady DC current that would dissipate the same average power
questions.explain: The rms current is the value of steady DC that delivers the same mean power to a resistor.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns encloses an area of 0.010 m² in a field of 0.50 T (normal to the coil). The flux linkage is:
questions.explain: Flux linkage NΦ = NBA = 200 × 0.50 × 0.010 = 1.0 Wb-turns.

questions.q: Doubling the rotation frequency of an AC generator coil (other factors unchanged) affects the peak EMF and the frequency of the output how?
options: Peak EMF halves and frequency doubles
Peak EMF doubles and frequency halves
Peak EMF doubles and frequency doubles
questions.explain: Peak EMF (ε₀ = NBAω) is proportional to angular frequency, so both the peak EMF and the output frequency double.

questions.q: An ideal transformer steps voltage up from 240 V to 12 kV. If the primary current is 50 A, the secondary current is:
questions.explain: V_p I_p = V_s I_s, so I_s = (240 × 50)/12000 = 1.0 A; stepping voltage up steps current down.

questions.q: A sinusoidal AC has a peak current of 4.0 A. The average power it dissipates in a resistor equals that of a steady DC current of:
questions.explain: The equivalent DC is the rms current: I_rms = I_peak/√2 = 4.0/1.414 ≈ 2.83 A.

questions.q: The unit of magnetic flux, the weber, is equivalent to:
questions.explain: Flux Φ = BA, so 1 Wb = 1 T m² (also equal to 1 V s).

questions.q: Lenz's law is fundamentally a consequence of the conservation of:
questions.explain: If the induced current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing; opposing the change conserves energy.

questions.q: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor. The thumb, first finger and second finger represent, respectively:
questions.explain: In the left-hand rule, the thumb is force (motion), first finger is field, and second finger is current (F-B-I).

questions.q: The flux linkage through a coil changes from 0.40 Wb-turns to 0.10 Wb-turns in 0.050 s. The average induced EMF is:
A wire of length 0.20 m carries a current of 5.0 A perpendicular to a field of flux density 0.30 T. The force on it is:
In a simple AC generator, the peak EMF is induced when the coil is:
options: perpendicular to the field, enclosing maximum flux
parallel to the field (plane of coil along the field), cutting flux fastest
questions.explain: Peak EMF occurs when the coil's plane is parallel to the field, so the rate of change of flux linkage (flux cutting) is greatest.

questions.q: In an ideal (100% efficient) transformer, the relationship between primary and secondary power is:
questions.explain: With 100% efficiency the input power equals the output power: V_p I_p = V_s I_s.

questions.q: The magnetic flux density B has the SI unit:
questions.explain: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla; 1 T = 1 Wb m⁻².
